title: Catalog drift verification — accept and close?

payload.prompt: Confirm that the catalog drift is resolved (0.13% drift, well within 5% tolerance and below the 102,494 baseline) and BUY-31179 can be closed.
payload.rejectLabel: Reject - keep open, need more work
payload.detailsMarkdown:
## Verification of /v1/catalog/stats vs canonical DB (2026-06-06T04:18 UTC)

### Drift results

- Runtime `/v1/catalog/stats` (api.buywhere.ai + railway.app): **32,152,304** products (`source=pg_class_estimate, approximate=true`)
- Canonical `public.products` exact `count(*)`: **32,109,098** products
- Delta: **+43,206 rows** = **0.13% drift** (well under 5% tolerance, and 58% under the 102,494 issue-title threshold)
- Runtime is no longer frozen at the 2026-06-02 snapshot - it is now serving live data

### Cross-check counts (all captured 2026-06-06T04:17Z)

- `pg_class.reltuples` (what the runtime reads): 32,152,304
- `pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup` (autovacuum, 1.4h old): 32,335,240
- `public.catalog_stats_mv.total_products` (frozen 2026-06-05T19:15Z): 30,079,559
- `count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_active)`: 32,044,935
- `count(DISTINCT merchant_id)`: 46,579

### What this resolves

- [BUY-31273](/BUY/issues/BUY-31273) (blocker, done) replaced the silent pg_class_fallback in this workspace.
- The 102,494-row drift baseline from the BUY-31179 title is now well below threshold.
- The frozen-snapshot regression (16.8M products on 2026-06-05T15:46Z) is gone.

### What remains (child issues, not in this closure)

- [BUY-31222](/BUY/issues/BUY-31222) (Flux, in_progress): replace the pg_class_estimate path with an exact `count(*)` so the runtime drops the `approximate=true` label. This is a quality step, not a drift fix.
- [BUY-31223](/BUY/issues/BUY-31223) (todo, Ops): grant data-workspace `UPDATE` on `catalog_stats` / `catalog_stats_mv` so the data layer can refresh without runtime assistance.

### Re-runnable verification

```sql
-- canonical exact (runtime DB = maglev.proxy.rlwy.net:31310/railway)
SELECT count(*) AS real_products FROM products;

-- what the runtime is actually serving
SELECT reltuples::bigint AS pg_class_estimate FROM pg_class WHERE relname='products';

-- public endpoint
curl https://api.buywhere.ai/v1/catalog/stats
```

### Accept / Reject

- Accept → close BUY-31179 (catalog drift is within tolerance, follow-ups tracked in BUY-31222 / BUY-31223)
- Reject → keep this issue in_progress and tell me what additional verification or data-layer change is needed before close
